Robot Doctor Autonomous

Path follower overshoots, oscillates, or runs away

Pedro Pathing / Road Runner misbehaves while following a path. Below are the 6 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 6 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does the localization test pass (push 48" forward → X ≈ 48, left → Y up, heading correct)? Run your library's localization test OpMode and push the robot by hand.
  • Pushing the robot forward by hand, does X go up (and pushing left, does Y go up)? Run your localization test and watch telemetry while you push.
  • On a stand, does each wheel spin "forward" when you command forward? Lift the robot so the wheels are off the ground and drive forward slowly. Every wheel should turn the way that would move the robot forward.
  • Does it reach the end of the path but overshoot or jitter around it? It gets there, just not cleanly.
  • If you spin in place a few times, do X and Y drift far from 0? Turn the robot several full circles in place and look at X/Y.
  • Does it still happen with a freshly charged battery? Swap to a battery straight off the charger and repeat the exact same thing.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Localization isn't accurate yet

A path follower can only be as good as its position estimate. Bad localization looks exactly like bad tuning.

How to fix it 30 min

  1. Tune localization before any follower or PID tuning.
  2. Run the localization test: push forward 48" and check X ≈ 48, push left and check Y goes up, spin and check heading.
  3. Only move on once every check passes.

Sources: Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting

2 Odometry pod direction is reversed

If a pod counts backward, position runs off the opposite way as soon as you move.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Run a localization test and push the robot by hand.
  2. Forward should make X go up, pushing left should make Y go up, and turning counter-clockwise should make heading go up.
  3. Reverse whichever pod is wrong (Pinpoint: setEncoderDirections).

Sources: Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting · goBILDA · Pinpoint user guide (PDF) · Pedro Pathing · Pinpoint tuning

3 A drive motor is reversed

Motors on opposite sides face opposite ways, so one side has to be reversed in code. One wrong direction makes the robot spin, drift, or strafe diagonally.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Put the robot on a stand and command every drive motor forward at low power, one at a time.
  2. Every wheel should spin so the robot would go forward. Reverse any motor that spins backward.
  3. Some gearboxes and kits (goBILDA Strafer, REV mecanum kit) flip the direction again through gearing, so test instead of guessing.
Reverse one side
frontLeft.setDirection(DcMotorSimple.Direction.REVERSE);
backLeft.setDirection(DcMotorSimple.Direction.REVERSE);
// test each wheel on its own if anything still looks off

Sources: GM0 · Mecanum teleop · Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting

4 Follower correction is too aggressive

Overshoot and jitter usually mean the translational or heading P is too high, or the static feedforward is too big.

How to fix it 45 min

  1. Work out which part is misbehaving: heading, forward, or sideways correction.
  2. Overshooting or jittery: lower that controller's P. Too lazy: raise it.
  3. A static feedforward that is too high also causes jitter and overshoot.
  4. Run the auto-tuners on a full battery, several times, and average the results.

Sources: Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting

5 Pod offsets are wrong or swapped

Offsets tell the localizer where each pod sits from the robot's turning center. Wrong ones show up as drift when the robot turns.

How to fix it 20 min

  1. Spin the robot in place several times. If X/Y wander far from 0, the offsets are off.
  2. Measure from the center of rotation and follow your library's sign convention exactly (Pinpoint: X offset is how far sideways the forward pod is, left positive; Y offset is how far forward the strafe pod is, forward positive).
  3. Make sure the forward and strafe pods are not swapped (Pinpoint: forward pod in the X port).
  4. Pedro Pathing's Pinpoint auto-tuner can measure offsets for you.

Sources: Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting · goBILDA · Pinpoint user guide (PDF) · Pedro Pathing · Pinpoint tuning

6 Battery is low or worn out

A tired battery sags under load, so motors slow down and the hub can brown out.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Swap in a freshly charged battery and test again. That alone answers the question.
  2. Watch the voltage on the Driver Station while you drive hard. Healthy packs dip, but sitting around 9 V or lower under load is a problem.
  3. Charge at the rate the battery maker recommends (REV slim: 1.8 A on the REV charger; TETRIX: 0.9 A).
  4. Label every battery with your team number, the year, and a name, and tally charge cycles. NiMH packs get weak after roughly 200–300 cycles.
  5. Retire packs that drop fast even when full. A battery tester (like a Battery Beak) shows internal resistance.

Sources: FTC Docs · Battery care, charging, fuses · REV · Control Hub troubleshooting · REV · 12V battery troubleshooting
